ov: Venomous reef fish of the Indo-Pacific with bold red, brown or black and white stripes and long, fan-like fins tipped with venomous spines. Probably released from aquariums, two species have become a major invasive pest in the western Atlantic, the Caribbean and the Mediterranean.

why.dg: Stings cause severe pain and can be fatal, mostly to young children, the elderly or people allergic to the venom; they are rarely fatal to healthy adults.
why.p: Popular aquarium fish, though they need an experienced keeper and are often sold to beginners who struggle with them.
why.et: Edible if prepared correctly; divers in Florida and Texas are encouraged to catch them for food to fight the invasion.
why.ac: Mostly nocturnal, active from nightfall through the night.

rg: Native to the Indian Ocean and western Pacific. Invasive along the US East Coast, in the Gulf of Mexico, the Caribbean, the Mediterranean and off Brazil.
df: Mostly crustaceans such as shrimps and crabs, plus small fish, swallowed whole in a single motion.
fx: A female can lay about 2 million eggs a year.
Moray eels, barracuda and large groupers have been seen eating lionfish.
